units.title: Rayleigh objective: remove the radial part of 2Ax
units.statement: For a symmetric linear operator A on a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space, let F(x)=⟨x,Ax⟩ on the unit sphere. With its induced metric, the unique ambient tangent vector representing the genuine sphere differential is Gₓ=2(Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x). More explicitly, every z in x⊥ represents that differential against every actual tangent direction exactly when z=Gₓ.
units.formula: \begin{gathered}F(x)=\langle x,Ax\rangle,\quad T_xS=x^\perp,\quad J_x=D\iota(x),\\ DF(x)[w]=\langle J_xw,z\rangle\ \forall w\ \Longleftrightarrow\ z=G_x\quad(z\in x^\perp),\\ G_x=2(Ax-\langle x,Ax\rangle x).\end{gathered}
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space of dimension n+1. In orthonormal coordinates A is the source real symmetric matrix; its continuous-linear-map representation adds no regularity assumption in finite dimension.
A is symmetric, not necessarily positive, positive definite or invertible. x has norm one. Nonzeroness of x and the Rayleigh eigenvalue identity are derived internally, not added hypotheses.

The objective is the literal sphere restriction F(x)=⟨x,Ax⟩ of the smooth quadratic q(y)=⟨y,Ay⟩. The ambient quotient is defined only for y≠0; its equality with this restriction uses ‖x‖=1. No derivative of an off-domain totalized quotient is used.

The metric is the ambient-induced one. The actual inclusion derivative Jₓ maps abstract chart directions into x⊥. Pairings with Jₓw express this induced metric explicitly; no default chart inner product is identified with it.

n may be zero. The claims are pointwise, with every x and every tangent test direction quantified. They neither construct a global gradient-field object nor claim a convergence or extremal-eigenvalue theorem.

steps.title: Differentiate the symmetric quadratic
steps.text: Expand q(x+tv). Symmetry makes the two first-order cross terms equal, giving Dq(x)[v]=2⟨Ax,v⟩ and hence the genuine ambient gradient 2Ax. The implementation reuses Mathlib’s derivative, proves that its quadratic is literally q, and identifies its linear functional with the gradient dual. No gradient witness is supplied by the reader.
steps.lean:
have hx : ‖(x : E)‖ = 1 := mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp x.property
  have hg : HasGradientAt (fun y : E => ⟪y, A y⟫_ℝ) ((2 : ℝ) • A (x : E)) (x : E) := by
    apply hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt.mpr
    have hraw := (hA.hasStrictFDerivAt_reApplyInnerSelf (x : E)).hasFDerivAt
    have hfun : (fun y : E => ⟪y, A y⟫_ℝ) = A.reApplyInnerSelf := by
      funext y
      simp [ContinuousLinearMap.reApplyInnerSelf_apply, real_inner_comm]
    have hlin : toDual ℝ E ((2 : ℝ) • A (x : E)) =
        (2 : ℕ) • innerSL ℝ (A (x : E)) := by
      ext v
      simp [toDual_apply_apply, two_smul]
    rw [hfun, hlin]
    exact hraw
steps.detail: The strict derivative API writes its coefficient as natural-number addition twice; two_smul identifies it with multiplication by the real scalar2. This is an API adapter, not a change of normalization.

steps.title: Project onto the actual tangent plane
steps.text: Because x is a unit vector, the projection onto its normal line sends u to ⟨x,u⟩x. Subtracting this normal component gives the projection onto x⊥. Apply this to 2Ax and use bilinearity to obtain the displayed vector Gₓ. In particular Gₓ is tangent: ⟨x,Gₓ⟩=2(⟨x,Ax⟩−⟨x,Ax⟩‖x‖²)=0.
steps.formula: P_{x^\perp}u=u-\langle x,u\rangle x,\qquad P_{x^\perp}(2Ax)=2(Ax-\langle x,Ax\rangle x).
steps.lean:
let K := (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ
  have hproj (u : E) : (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto u : E) =
      u - ⟪(x : E), u⟫_ℝ • (x : E) := by
    change (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ.starProjection u = _
    rw [Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_val,
      Submodule.starProjection_unit_singleton ℝ hx]
  have hp : (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto ((2 : ℝ) • A (x : E)) : E) =
      (2 : ℝ) • (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) := by
    rw [hproj]
    simp [inner_smul_right, smul_sub, smul_smul]
steps.detail: Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_val and starProjection_unit_singleton supply the exact projection formula. The local hproj holds for every ambient u and covers source equation3.40; no duplicate public projection lemma is introduced.

steps.title: Use the induced differential characterization
steps.text: The existing genuine-sphere theorem applies to the actual ambient gradient just proved. The inclusion chain rule and its exact tangent range are already established in that parent: the restricted differential pairs with a tangent candidate precisely when it is the orthogonal projection. Replacing that projection by Gₓ gives the claimed formula and uniqueness. Existence uses the projected vector in x⊥, not an assumed solution.
steps.lean:
intro z
  rw [SphereGradient.sphere_gradient_characterization n x hg z]
  constructor
  · intro hz
    exact (congrArg (fun v : K => (v : E)) hz).trans hp
  · intro hz
    apply Subtype.ext
    exact hz.trans hp.symm
steps.detail: The canonical SphereGradient.sphere_gradient_characterization supplies the true nonlinear differential and uniqueness. Subtype.ext and congrArg only move the already tangent projection between its subtype and ambient representation.

units.lean_statement: All source data are quantified. z is typed in the ambient tangent plane x⊥, w in the actual Mathlib TangentSpace. The inclusion differential Jₓ transports w into the ambient space for the exact induced pairing. The iff yields the explicit unique representative; it is not a definition of a new gradient field.
units.lean_proof: Produce the true quadratic derivative, compute the unit tangent projection and apply the existing canonical sphere differential theorem.

units.title: Sphere stationary points are exactly unit eigenvectors
units.statement: For the same symmetric quadratic on the induced unit sphere, the genuine manifold differential at x is zero exactly when Ax=⟨x,Ax⟩x, and exactly when x is an eigenvector of A. If Ax=μx, the unit norm forces μ=⟨x,Ax⟩. Zero or negative eigenvalues are allowed.
units.formula: \begin{gathered}DF(x)=0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ Ax=\langle x,Ax\rangle x\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \exists\mu\in\mathbb R:\ Ax=\mu x,\ x\ne0,\\ Ax=\mu x\Rightarrow\mu=\langle x,Ax\rangle.\end{gathered}
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space of dimension n+1. In orthonormal coordinates A is the source real symmetric matrix; its continuous-linear-map representation adds no regularity assumption in finite dimension.
A is symmetric, not necessarily positive, positive definite or invertible. x has norm one. Nonzeroness of x and the Rayleigh eigenvalue identity are derived internally, not added hypotheses.

The objective is the literal sphere restriction F(x)=⟨x,Ax⟩ of the smooth quadratic q(y)=⟨y,Ay⟩. The ambient quotient is defined only for y≠0; its equality with this restriction uses ‖x‖=1. No derivative of an off-domain totalized quotient is used.

The metric is the ambient-induced one. The actual inclusion derivative Jₓ maps abstract chart directions into x⊥. Pairings with Jₓw express this induced metric explicitly; no default chart inner product is identified with it.

n may be zero. The claims are pointwise, with every x and every tangent test direction quantified. They neither construct a global gradient-field object nor claim a convergence or extremal-eigenvalue theorem.

steps.title: Turn zero differential into zero projected gradient
steps.text: A continuous linear differential is zero exactly when it vanishes on every tangent direction. The first theorem at the candidate z=0 says that these vanishing pairings hold precisely when Gₓ=0. This explicitly implements the source-derived bridge from differential stationarity to induced-gradient stationarity. Cancel the nonzero real scalar2 and rearrange the difference.
steps.formula: DF(x)=0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ DF(x)[w]=0\ \forall w\ \Longleftrightarrow\ 0=2(Ax-\langle x,Ax\rangle x)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ Ax=\langle x,Ax\rangle x.
steps.lean:
have hx : ‖(x : E)‖ = 1 := mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp x.property
  have hxne : (x : E) ≠ 0 := by
    intro hz
    simp [hz] at hx
  have hzero := sphere_rayleigh_characterization n A hA x 0
  have hd :
      mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
        A (x : E) = ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E) := by
    have he :
        mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x = 0 ↔
          ∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
            mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x w = 0 := by
      constructor
      · intro h w
        rw [h]
        rfl
      · intro h
        ext w
        exact h w
    rw [he]
    have hs : (0 : E) = (2 : ℝ) •
        (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) ↔
          A (x : E) = ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E) := by
      rw [eq_comm, smul_eq_zero, sub_eq_zero]
      simp
    have hpair :
        (∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
          mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x w = 0) ↔
          (0 : E) = (2 : ℝ) • (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)) := by
      simpa only [Submodule.coe_zero, inner_zero_right] using hzero
    exact hpair.trans hs
steps.detail: The proof uses extensionality of the actual differential, not an arbitrary supplied pairing identity. The characterization tests every chart direction through the canonical induced pairing. Norm one gives x≠0 internally.

steps.title: A stationary unit vector is an eigenvector
steps.text: The preceding equality puts x in the eigenspace with eigenvalue ⟨x,Ax⟩. Unit membership proves x≠0, so this is genuine eigenvectorhood in the library sense rather than the equation alone, which would also hold at zero.
steps.formula: Ax=\langle x,Ax\rangle x,\quad\|x\|=1\Rightarrow x\ne0,\qquad x\in E_{\langle x,Ax\rangle}(A)\setminus\{0\}.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨hd, ?_⟩
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact ⟨⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ,
      Module.End.mem_eigenspace_iff.mpr (hd.mp h), hxne⟩
steps.detail: Module.End.mem_eigenspace_iff supplies eigenspace membership; HasEigenvector includes the proved nonzeroness. No spectral existence theorem or positivity assumption is needed.

steps.title: Every unit eigenvector is stationary
steps.text: Conversely, suppose Ax=μx. Pair with x to get ⟨x,Ax⟩=μ‖x‖²=μ. Thus the eigenvector equation is exactly the Rayleigh-coefficient equation, and the first equivalence gives DF(x)=0. This proves the converse for any real eigenvalue, including zero and negative values.
steps.formula: \langle x,Ax\rangle=\langle x,\mu x\rangle=\mu\|x\|^2=\mu,\qquad Ax=\langle x,Ax\rangle x\Rightarrow DF(x)=0.
steps.lean:
· rintro ⟨μ, hμ⟩
    have hAx : A (x : E) = μ • (x : E) := hμ.apply_eq_smul
    have hcoef : ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ = μ := by
      rw [hAx, inner_smul_right]
      simp [hx]
    apply hd.mpr
    rw [hcoef]
    exact hAx
steps.detail: HasEigenvector.apply_eq_smul gives the actual eigenvalue equation. The coefficient identity uses the source unit norm; it is not added as a theorem hypothesis.

units.lean_statement: The first conjunct identifies a zero continuous-linear-map differential with the Rayleigh equation. The second conjunct identifies it with an existential actual Module.End.HasEigenvector. All x on the unit sphere are quantified, and no nonzero-eigenvalue premise is present.
units.lean_proof: Evaluate the genuine gradient characterization at zero; derive the coefficient equation; construct the actual eigenvector and prove the converse by unit normalization.
